Q: Big O (time complexity) calculation A:

For each value of i and j, the value of k will increment approximately N/(i+j+5) times. Since values of j increase as powers of 2, altogether this gives ∑i=0N(∑j=0log N N/(i+2j+5)) iterations. The sums over i and j can be interchanged, which gives ∑j=0log N (N*(∑i=0N 1/(i+2j+5))). The inner sum is a partial sum of the harmonic series, so it can be approximated by log(N + 2j) - log(2j) = log(1 + N/2j) = log(1+2(log N - j)) ≈ log(2(log N - j)) = log N -j. The double sum is then approximately equal to N*(∑j=0log N (log N -j)) ≈ N*(log N)*(log N + 1)/2 ≈N*log(N)2/2. Which gives complexity O(N*log(N)2).

Q: How to document / annotate scope of end-to-end browser tests? A:

You have coverage tools for playwright / cypress.io / et similia, but I don't think they really measure anything like coverage for unit tests do.

What I personally do is to curate a .md document in the repo where I summarize all the existing tests and the missing ones, with a rationale if possible.

E2E tests have the most value since they test what your actual users experience, at the price of:

  • taking longer to write;
  • taking (a lot) longer to execute;
  • being the easiest to break.

Given normal time / budget constraints you cannot test every single code branch so you have to make choices:

As a contrived example, assume I would want to write a end-to-end-test for stackoverflow itself. I want to focus on the flow "a user asks a question". Yet due to time contraints I only implement the question type "troubleshooting", not the other types like "best practices", or "general advice / other", etc. Also, my test case only adds one tag, as it is a required field, but I don't test the behavior for more than one tag, I don't test the limit of at most five tags, or adding and removing tags.

You can e2e test that asking a question makes it appear on the applied tag question list, makes it appear when searching for it, and the data is correctly rendered on the single question page.

All the tags behaviours can be unit / integration tested, since they are not critical.

For instance you can just do:

id = createQuestion(..., tags = [A, B])
searchForTag(A) // contains id
editQuestion(id, tags = [B])
searchForTag(A) // does not contain id

At db / orm / api level and living with it.

Q: System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException: 'No installed components were detected A:

I know this is almost two years old at this point, but in case any one else stumbles on this. A control can only have one parent and you are adding dlog to stackmain twice.

From CreateDailyLogUI you call CreateScrollView.

In CreateScrollView you initialize stackmain and define the children, of which dlog is included.

At the end of CreateDailyLogUI, you call SetModelBinding, which attempts to add dlog to StackMain again, which is where you are getting your error.

You need to pick the one that works best for your scenario.

Q: How to uninstall the exact LLVM and CLANG version on Linux A:

If apt-get purge doesn't work in your case, which it didn't for me, then you may benefit from the following approach.

Use whereis to determine the location of your default LLVM and clang. In my case, this was /usr/local/bin.

Remove your old version of LLVM, Clang and their auxiliary tooling with a simple rm -f /usr/local/bin/clang* and likewise with the path /usr/local/bin/llvm*

I'll follow up here with how to bind the clang* and llvm-* commands to the version you want to use by default. In my case this was version 20, so adjust as needed.

  1. sudo apt install llvm-<version-number>

  2. Use update-alternatives to set your desired version of LLVM and clang like so:

sudo update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/clang clang /usr/bin/clang-20 200 \
                         --slave /usr/bin/clang++ clang++ /usr/bin/clang++-20 \
                         --slave /usr/bin/llvm-config llvm-config /usr/bin/llvm-config-20

If this doesn't work for your specific setup, or you need assistance, let me know.

Q: Does VB.Net have an equivalent to #pragma warning disable/restore? A:

If you are using Visual Studio 2015, the answer is yes, yes it does. The syntax is #Disable Warning BC40000 and #Enable Warning BC40000

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/visual-basic/language-reference/directives/disable-enable
